root_cause: Text.expand_tabs rebuilt the text by appending each tab-terminated part and then appending the padding spaces with the Text's base style (_style = self.style), so any span that covered the tab character stopped at the single replaced space and the padding was unstyled. It also computed tab stops from len() (code points) instead of cell_len, so wide chars (emoji) got the wrong padding, and Text.append/append_text/append_tokens used `if style is not None`, so appending parts whose style is '' (from_markup/blank_copy default) emitted spurious Span(a, b, '') entries.
best_solution: In rich/text.py: (1) add Span.extend(cells) returning Span(start, end+cells, style) (self if cells==0); (2) add Text.extend_style(spaces): no-op if spaces<=0, else append ' '*spaces and extend every span whose end >= len(self) by spaces (plain += spaces when there are no spans); (3) rewrite expand_tabs per line: lines without a tab are kept as-is; otherwise split on '\t' with include_separator, replace the trailing tab of a part with ' ' in part._text[-1], advance cell_position by part.cell_len, and if cell_position % tab_size != 0 call part.extend_style(tab_size - remainder); collect parts and rebuild with Text('').join(parts), then copy plain/_spans back into self; (4) change `if style is not None` / `if text.style is not None` to truthiness checks in append, append_text and append_tokens so '' styles produce no span; (5) Text.tab_size defaults to None and __rich_console__ uses console.tab_size when self.tab_size is None. Reasoning from the statement: 'extend the style(s) on the tab to cover the new space characters' means grow the existing spans that end at the tab (all of them, since overlapping styles like red+green both apply), not create a new span with one chosen style; tab stops are measured in terminal cells.
acceptable_alternatives: Any expand_tabs implementation that yields exactly the same span lists (spans split at tab-part boundaries, every span ending at the tab extended, no '' spans, cell_len tab stops) plus a public Text.extend_style(spaces) with the tested semantics would pass. The `is not None` -> truthiness change in append* is required, because test_panel.test_render_size now expects the title row as one merged Segment and all tab span tests expect no Span(..., '').
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_text.py::test_tabs_to_spaces (Text('No Tabs', style='bold') keeps style), test_tabs_to_spaces_spans (12 parametrized cases asserting exact text._spans lists, e.g. '[bold]foo\tbar' tab 4 -> [Span(0,4,'bold'), Span(4,7,'bold')]; '[red]foo\tbar\n[green]egg\tbaz' tab 8 -> both red and green spans extended to 12-20; '[bold]💩\t💩' tab 8 -> '💩      💩' with Span(0,7) i.e. cell_len-based stops; '\t' with no markup -> [] no empty-style spans), test_extend_style (new method Text.extend_style: 0 and -1 are no-ops, extend_style(2) on '[red]foo[/red] [bold]bar' gives 'foo bar  ' and Span(4,9,'bold')), tests/test_panel.py::test_render_size (title row rendered as a single Segment, a consequence of not emitting '' spans).
locating_signals: Statement names `Text.extend_tabs` (the real method is Text.expand_tabs in rich/text.py; grep 'tabs' in text.py finds it). It says nothing about Span.extend, Text.extend_style, cell_len, the append `is not None` change, or tab_size default; those are only in the CHANGELOG of the PR ('Added Text.extend_style method', 'Added Span.extend method').
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env (v4 136s/100 calls, v6 120s/49, v7 97s/46, v8 138s/47). v4 and v8 made the same one-line change, padding with `part.style` instead of `_style`; part.style is the whole Text's base style copied by split, not the span on the tab, so styled tabs stay unstyled. v6 and v7 looked for a span covering the tab and appended the padding as a new span with that single style (last match wins), so overlapping styles are lost. None of the four switched tab stops to cell_len (emoji cases fail), stopped emitting Span(..., '') from append (every exact-span test and test_panel fail), or added Text.extend_style (AttributeError). v4 log: 12 failed, 100 passed. v6/v7/v8 also added stray test files under tests/.
generalizable_lesson: When hidden tests may compare exact internal structures (span lists, segment lists), a minimal patch at the obvious line is not enough. Trace the full data flow for the simplest inputs in the statement (unstyled, one styled, overlapping styles, wide or unicode characters), print the resulting internal structure, and remove spurious artifacts such as empty-style entries. When the statement's verb phrase suggests a helper ("extend the style"), add a small public helper with that name (extend_style / Span.extend) instead of inlining the logic. Measure text width with the library's display-width function (cell_len), not len().
